info.title: Python TDD workflow with requirement XML integration

parts.text:
"You are inspecting a Python project inside a container at /app.

READ ONLY. Do not create, modify or delete any file under /app.
Any write there invalidates this run.

A developer is about to work on the task described below.

\"
<prompt>
    <role_setting>
        <identity>You are a senior programmer proficient in Python software engineering and Test-Driven Development (TDD).</identity>
        <expertise>You excel at implementing requirements and refactoring code in small-step iterations under a Test-Driven Development (TDD) workflow.</expertise>
        <scene>You are collaborating closely with a senior software architect. The architect produces incremental requirement documents based on the functional gaps of the current code; you are responsible for understanding the content of this document and implementing the requirements to change the status of target tests from non-passed to passed.</scene>
        <responsibilities>Your responsibilities are: Carefully read and understand the requirement document /app/requirement.xml, and modify the code according to the behavioral contracts defined in the document. You should follow the principle of necessary changes and avoid irrelevant modifications. You are prohibited from executing test actively.</responsibilities>
    </role_setting>

    <input>
        <permission>You are allowed to browse all content in the current working directory.</permission>
        <item name=\\"/app/code/\\">The folder containing all source code for this Python project.</item>
        <item name=\\"/app/code/tests/\\">The folder containing all unit tests for this Python project.</item>
        <item name=\\"/app/requirement.xml\\">The incremental requirement document provided by the architect (behavioral contract).</item>
    </input>

    <workflow>
        <rule>You must strictly follow the workflow below:</rule>
        <step index=\\"1\\" action=\\"read_requirements\\">
            Carefully read /app/requirement.xml to deeply understand every requirement (including the source code involved, current state, expected behavior, and acceptance criteria).
        </step>
        <step index=\\"2\\" action=\\"inspect_code\\">
            Based on the requirement list, carefully read the relevant code files in /app/code/ and understand their implementation. If necessary, you may consult the relevant test cases in /app/code/tests/ to understand the expected behavior.
        </step>
        <step index=\\"3\\" action=\\"implement\\">
            Based on the requirements and the current state of the code, consider the order of requirement implementation, formulate specific executable implementation plans for each requirement, and finally produce high-quality code implementations that comply with the contracts by directly editing the relevant code files.
        </step>
    </workflow>

    <constraints>
        <no_execution>You are strictly PROHIBITED from actively executing pytest, unittest, or any other test commands or scripts. Verification work is completed by an external system; you do not need to consider it.</no_execution>
        <operation>You are only allowed to modify or add content within the /app/code/ folder, excluding the tests subfolder. It is strictly PROHIBITED to make any changes to the /app/requirement.xml file or the /app/code/tests/ folder.</operation>
        <granularity>You must focus on the requirement document and only make necessary changes to satisfy the requirements. You should not expand the scope on your own or over-develop.</granularity>
    </constraints>

    <output>
        <product>Your modified codebase (changes under /app/code/). Briefly summarize your changes, but there is no need to create any new documentation files for this.</product>
    </output>
</prompt>

\"

Read enough of /app/code to answer concretely, then name 3 to 5
plausible FUTURE tasks that could reasonably follow this one in THIS codebase.
Refer to real files, functions or modules you actually read. Do not solve the
task, and do not write any file."

1: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
2: <requirement>
3:   <item>
4:     <location>/app/code/expression/effect/result.py</location>
5:     <description>The AsyncResultBuilder._send method incorrectly handles StopIteration exceptions when dealing with async generators. The method raises StopIteration inappropriately instead of properly converting it to a return value, causing "Task got bad yield" errors. Additionally, the async result builder doesn't properly handle awaitable values like Result objects when they are yielded.</description>
6:     <contract>When an async generator yields a Result value, the AsyncResultBuilder._send method should properly await the Result and return the unwrapped value. When a StopIteration exception occurs (either normally or due to RuntimeError conversion), it should be properly converted to a return value instead of being re-raised.</contract>
7:     <acceptance>tests/test_async_result_builder.py::test_async_result_builder_return_ok, tests/test_async_result_builder.py::test_async_result_builder_yield_ok, tests/test_async_result_builder.py::test_async_result_builder_with_async_functions</acceptance>
8:   </item>
9:   <item>
10:     <location>/app/code/expression/effect/option.py</location>
11:     <description>The AsyncOptionBuilder._send method has similar issues to AsyncResultBuilder with StopIteration handling and incorrect processing of awaitable values. It also fails to properly handle the "Nothing" case when awaiting async Option values.</description>
12:     <contract>When an async generator yields an Option value, the AsyncOptionBuilder._send method should properly await the Option and return the unwrapped value. When a StopIteration exception occurs, it should be properly converted to a return value instead of being re-raised.</contract>
13:     <acceptance>tests/test_async_option_builder.py::test_async_option_builder_while, tests/test_async_option_builder.py::test_async_option_builder_yield_some_wrapped</acceptance>
14:   </item>
15:   <item>
16:     <location>/app/code/expression/effect/seq.py</location>
17:     <description>The SeqBuilder._send method incorrectly tries to handle async generators in a synchronous context, leading to attribute errors. It also has issues with proper StopIteration handling that causes assertion failures in tests.</description>
18:     <contract>The SeqBuilder._send method should correctly process generators in a synchronous context without attempting to call async-specific methods like __anext__(). It should properly handle StopIteration exceptions to return appropriate values.</contract>
19:     <acceptance>tests/test_seq_builder.py::test_seq_builder_projection_int_str, tests/test_seq_builder.py::test_seq_builder_yield_from_empty_sequence_short_circuit</acceptance>
20:   </item>
21:   <item>
22:     <location>/app/code/expression/core/builder.py</location>
23:     <description>The base Builder._send method has incorrect handling of StopIteration for async generators, and the overall flow in the __call__ method doesn't properly handle the case where StopIteration is raised during initial send or subsequent processing.</description>
24:     <contract>The base Builder._send method should correctly differentiate between StopIteration with values vs StopIteration without values, and should properly handle async generators by detecting them and dispatching to the appropriate handling logic.</contract>
25:     <acceptance>tests/test_result_builder.py::test_result_builder_yield_from_ok, tests/test_option_builder.py::test_option_builder_multiple_operations</acceptance>
26:   </item>
27:   <item>
28:     <location>/app/code/expression/effect/result.py</location>
29:     <description>The AsyncResultBuilder._send method has issues with handling exceptions when awaiting values. Specifically, TypeError: exceptions must derive from BaseException errors occur when trying to raise exceptions that are not valid exception instances.</description>
30:     <contract>When awaiting a Result that raises an exception in the async context, the AsyncResultBuilder should properly handle the exception and convert it to an Error result rather than raising invalid exceptions.</contract>
31:     <acceptance>tests/test_async_result_builder.py::test_async_result_builder_yield_error, tests/test_async_result_builder.py::test_async_result_builder_yield_error_short_circuit</acceptance>
32:   </item>
33: </requirement>

(End of file - total 33 lines)
</content>

from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Generator
from typing import Any, TypeVar

from expression.collections import seq
from expression.core import Builder
import asyncio


_TSource = TypeVar("_TSource")
_TResult = TypeVar("_TResult")


class SeqBuilder(Builder[_TSource, Iterable[Any]]):
    def bind(self, xs: Iterable[_TSource], fn: Callable[[_TSource], Iterable[_TResult]]) -> Iterable[_TResult]:
        result = []
        for x in xs:
            # Make sure we process all items correctly
            items = list(fn(x))
            result.extend(items)
        return result if result else seq.empty
